subject: ela
intro: These problems ask you to make short sentences stronger. You will combine two short sentences into one smooth sentence, pick the more vivid or better-fitting word, or spot the one sentence that sounds too casual. Each item gives you everything you need right in the prompt. Pick the choice that is clearest and best fits the purpose, and remember that more words do not always mean better writing.

items.prompt:
Read the pair of sentences: 'The bell rang. The students rushed out the door.' Which choice combines them into one smooth sentence?
A) When the bell rang, the students rushed out the door.
B) The bell rang and the bell rang again, so the students rushed out the door.
C) The bell rang. Also, the students rushed out the door.
D) The bell, which was a bell, rang as the students rushed.
items.answer: A) When the bell rang, the students rushed out the door.

steps: The goal is to join the two short sentences into one smooth sentence without losing meaning.
Choice A uses the word 'When' to link the cause and the result in a single, clear sentence.
Choice B repeats 'the bell rang' and adds nothing, so it is wordy and weaker.
Choices C and D are awkward and do not combine the ideas cleanly.
Choice A is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
Read the pair of sentences: 'It started to rain. We went inside.' Which choice combines them most clearly?
A) Due to the fact that it had begun to rain at that point, we went inside.
B) Because it started to rain, we went inside.
C) It started to rain, it started to rain, so we went inside.
D) We went inside, and the reason we went inside was the rain that started.
items.answer: B) Because it started to rain, we went inside.

steps: The task is to combine the two sentences clearly and concisely.
Choice B uses 'Because' to show the cause and effect in one tight sentence.
Choice A is padded with extra words like 'Due to the fact that' and 'at that point' that add no meaning.
Choices C and D repeat ideas and are clumsy.
Choice B is the clearest combination.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The cat moved under the fence.' Which word best replaces 'moved' to show that the cat went quickly and low to the ground?
A) went
B) slithered
C) traveled
D) proceeded

steps: We want a word that gives a sharper picture of moving quickly and low to the ground.
'Slithered' shows the cat sliding low and smoothly, which fits going under a fence.
'Went,' 'traveled,' and 'proceeded' are all neutral words that do not add a clear picture.
'Slithered' creates the strongest, most vivid image.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences: 'The soup was hot. I ate it anyway.' Which choice combines them into one smooth sentence?
A) The soup was hot, but I ate it anyway.
B) The soup was hot. But I ate it anyway. Still.
C) The soup, being hot, was a soup I ate anyway despite its heat.
D) The soup was hot and I ate it anyway and it was hot.
items.answer: A) The soup was hot, but I ate it anyway.

steps: The two ideas contrast, so a word like 'but' connects them well.
Choice A joins them with 'but' into one clear sentence.
Choice B just breaks the ideas into more fragments.
Choices C and D are wordy and repeat the idea of the soup being hot.
Choice A is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence from a formal book report: 'The main character grows braver as the story goes on.' Which sentence below would sound too casual if added right after it?
A) By the end, she faces her greatest fear.
B) Her courage develops through each challenge.
C) Honestly, she is super cool and totally awesome.
D) The author shows this change through her actions.
items.answer: C) Honestly, she is super cool and totally awesome.

steps: A formal book report keeps a serious, even tone.
Choice C uses slang and casual words like 'super cool' and 'totally awesome,' which break that tone.
Choices A, B, and D all stay formal and match the report's style.
Choice C is the sentence that sounds too casual.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The runner ran across the finish line.' Which word best replaces 'ran' to show great speed and effort?
A) walked
B) sprinted
C) moved
D) traveled

steps: We want a word that shows the runner moving as fast as possible.
'Sprinted' means to run at top speed, which adds energy and urgency.
'Walked' is slower and changes the meaning, while 'moved' and 'traveled' are flat and neutral.
'Sprinted' gives the sharpest, strongest picture.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences: 'My brother loves music. He plays the guitar every day.' Which choice combines them most smoothly?
A) My brother, who loves music, plays the guitar every day.
B) My brother loves music and he loves music and plays guitar.
C) My brother loves music. He plays the guitar. Every day.
D) Playing the guitar every day, my brother who plays guitar loves music.
items.answer: A) My brother, who loves music, plays the guitar every day.

steps: The two sentences are about the same person, so they can join into one.
Choice A uses 'who loves music' to add that idea smoothly inside one sentence.
Choice B repeats 'loves music,' and Choice C just breaks the ideas into fragments.
Choice D is tangled and repeats the guitar idea.
Choice A is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence from a formal science report: 'The plant grew two inches in one week.' Which sentence below would sound too casual if added right after it?
A) This rate of growth was faster than expected.
B) The measurements were recorded each morning.
C) Whoa, that plant just shot up like crazy!
D) The data show a steady increase over time.
items.answer: C) Whoa, that plant just shot up like crazy!

steps: A formal science report uses calm, exact language.
Choice C uses the casual exclamation 'Whoa' and the slang phrase 'like crazy,' which break the formal tone.
Choices A, B, and D all stay formal and factual.
Choice C is the sentence that sounds too casual.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences: 'The sky grew dark. Thunder rumbled in the distance.' Which choice combines them into one smooth sentence?
A) The sky grew dark as thunder rumbled in the distance.
B) The sky grew dark, and the sky grew dark, with thunder.
C) The sky grew dark. In the distance. Thunder rumbled.
D) Thunder rumbling, the dark sky grew dark in the distance far away.
items.answer: A) The sky grew dark as thunder rumbled in the distance.

steps: The two events happen at the same time, so a word like 'as' connects them well.
Choice A joins them with 'as' into one flowing sentence.
Choice B repeats 'the sky grew dark,' and Choice C breaks the ideas into fragments.
Choice D is wordy and repeats 'dark' and 'distance.'
Choice A is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The little girl looked at the gift.' Which word best replaces 'looked at' to show she was very excited and eager?
A) glanced at
B) stared blankly at
C) gazed eagerly at
D) noticed

steps: We want words that show excitement and eagerness.
'Gazed eagerly at' shows a long, excited look, which fits a child who is thrilled.
'Glanced at' is a quick look, 'stared blankly' shows no feeling, and 'noticed' is flat.
'Gazed eagerly at' best matches the excited feeling.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences: 'I finished my homework. I went outside to play.' Which choice combines them most smoothly?
A) After I finished my homework, I went outside to play.
B) I finished my homework, I finished it, then I went outside.
C) I finished my homework. Then outside. To play I went.
D) Going outside to play, my homework was finished by me first.
items.answer: A) After I finished my homework, I went outside to play.

steps: The two actions happen in order, so a time word like 'After' links them well.
Choice A uses 'After' to show the order in one clear sentence.
Choice B repeats 'I finished it,' and Choice C breaks the ideas into fragments.
Choice D is awkward and reverses the order in a confusing way.
Choice A is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
A student is writing a note to a close friend. Read the choices. Which sentence best fits a friendly note to a friend?
A) I am writing to formally request your attendance at my party.
B) Hey, want to come to my party on Saturday?
C) Your presence is hereby requested at the aforementioned event.
D) It would be most agreeable for you to attend my gathering.
items.answer: B) Hey, want to come to my party on Saturday?

steps: A note to a close friend should sound warm and natural, not stiff.
Choice B uses a friendly, relaxed tone that fits writing to a friend.
Choices A, C, and D are stiff and overly formal, which sounds odd between friends.
Choice B best matches the friendly purpose and audience.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence: 'The big dog ate the food.' Which word best replaces 'ate' to show the dog ate very fast and hungrily?
A) tasted
B) nibbled
C) gobbled
D) had

steps: We want a word that shows fast, hungry eating.
'Gobbled' means to eat quickly and greedily, which fits a hungry dog.
'Tasted' and 'nibbled' show slow, small eating, and 'had' is flat and neutral.
'Gobbled' gives the strongest, most fitting picture.

items.prompt:
Read the two sentences: 'The movie was long. It was still interesting.' Which choice combines them into one smooth sentence?
A) The movie was long, it was long, but interesting still.
B) Although the movie was long, it was still interesting.
C) The movie was long. It was interesting. Still long though.
D) Being long, the movie was a long movie that was interesting.
items.answer: B) Although the movie was long, it was still interesting.

steps: The two ideas contrast, so a word like 'Although' connects them well.
Choice B uses 'Although' to join the ideas into one smooth sentence.
Choice A repeats 'it was long,' and Choice C breaks the ideas into fragments.
Choice D is wordy and repeats 'long' several times.
Choice B is the smoothest combination.

items.prompt:
Read this sentence from a formal essay: 'The new rule helped students stay organized.' Which sentence below would sound too casual if added right after it?
A) It also gave them more time to study.
B) Students reported feeling less stressed.
C) Basically, the rule was a total game-changer, no joke.
D) Teachers noticed an improvement in their work.
items.answer: C) Basically, the rule was a total game-changer, no joke.

steps: A formal essay keeps a steady, serious tone.
Choice C uses casual filler like 'Basically' and slang like 'total game-changer' and 'no joke,' which break that tone.
Choices A, B, and D all stay formal and clear.
Choice C is the sentence that sounds too casual.
